title: Reading Drill — Changing where school buses stop — Preparing a second trial
description: One short passage, six questions. Recommended time: 10 minutes.

passages.title: Changing where school buses stop — Preparing a second trial
passages.body:
**A** In Millcross, work on children crossing an entrance used by staff cars had already produced a small collection of arrival observations. The school transport committee used this material to plan a second trial. The first report contained several different figures, but for the second trial the group agreed to publish one main outcome: conflicts between walkers and drivers.

**B** The group kept an alternate drop-off point for the new trial, which was planned to run for three weeks. Volunteers were shown a sample record before starting. They were also asked to describe anything unusual in a separate note, so later readers could tell the difference between an ordinary value and one taken during a disruption.

**C** The trial design stated that special events should be recorded even when everything else appeared normal. If this information was missing, the team would leave the field blank rather than infer an answer. It would publish a provisional finding and label it clearly if too few readings were available for a reliable result.
